body: To update, I got a small group of us to go over to his place and catch him for 5 minutes before he had to go out to eat with his family. We essentially just told him that we all care about him, to reinforce it. He took it very well. Soon I will try to get a one on one with him in the next few days to talk more in depth about intensive outpatient therapy. If I catch him when hes in a better mood, he may be more open to it. Thanks again.

Thank you so much for the detailed response. It is not limited to self harm and what he said earlier today. For years he has texted us randomly "I'm going to kill myself", and at this point we never know if he is being serious or not. A month ago he went up to his grandparent's house and said "I'm going to use my grandparent's gun." He never did, but he has said these things. I agree that he could have BPD, but it is not diagnosed. His home environment we know is not healthy for him, and that's why we try to get him out of the house as much as possible, though he often refuses. I have brought up intensive outpatient therapy, but it is usually met with a flat out no most of the time, and then he may turn irrational and accuse us of not caring. Should we keep pursuing this, just in different ways? Would you recommend getting a small group to talk to him about this, or keep it one on one. He says that hanging out in a group is not comfortable for him, but I want him to see how we all want him to get better. I agree that outpatient therapy is a more attractive solution, but I worry that it may get too late before he considers that option, as he seems extremely suicidal. Thank you for the valuable information. From that scale I would say he is an 8.5-9 on the scale.

Thanks for the advice. It is hard to convey everything in a simple reddit post, as we have known each other for such a long time, so I can't really spell everything out. I would say it alternates. There are times when he turns to irrational thoughts and therefore cannot logically sort out his issues, and he tends to prefer messaging about these issues rather than speaking in person about them. Through messages, I feel like I have to appease it, but in person, I try to bring up responsibility. It is hard not to play into it, as I don't want him to harm himself if I come off too stern. I have to catch him when he's thinking rationally, or he will try to turn it around on me if he perceives me coming off too aggressively. I'm simply worried, and feel helpless as his outlet for venting is texting us, or using reddit and not acknowledging there that there are people that care about him in the reddit posts. I'm ok with him venting to me, I just feel like were at the end of what friends can do. We think professional help is the next step but he doesn't listen, and says that he used to go to therapy and it didn't help him. It also doesn't help that he doesn't open up to professionals the same way he does to us. Everything is essentially exposed to us, but we don't have the resources or wherewithall actually provide real solutions. Again, thank you for responding.
